question: Five Tinkham Peak routes (East, North, Northwest Ridge, Southeast Spur, West) are indistinguishable; the common outing is the Mirror Lake loop. Which rows are real and distinct?
answer: Only two lines are documented, and they join into the common loop. Tinkham has two summits about 0.4 mile apart joined by an easy ridge: the WEST summit is the true high point (5,398-5,402 ft) and the EAST summit is a little lower (5,393-5,395 ft). (1) Northwest Ridge: from the Mirror Lake trail, the Cottonwood Lake spur and the Pacific Crest Trail, go north on the PCT to where a boot path leaves on the left and climbs the steep forested northwest ridge, with one short Class 3 gully or ledge near the top, to the west summit. This is the only route with a SummitPost route page and it is our one row that has text. (2) Southeast spur: from the south end of Mirror Lake, a steep boot path climbs the southeast spur through grass and talus to the EAST summit (about 1,200 ft in a bit over a mile from the lake, Class 2); it is easier and avoids the Class 3 gully; SummitPost has a route page for it too. The ridge between the summits is a walk (a few minutes), and the standard day is up one, across, down the other (about 6 miles and 2,200 ft round trip). Nothing I found documents a separate 'West Route', 'North Route' or 'East Route': every log is either 'Tinkham East' / 'boot trail' (the southeast spur), 'PCT' (the northwest ridge) or a longer Silver-Abiel-Tinkham link-up. So: East Route = Southeast Spur (same target, same boot path, 'Tinkham East' logs); North Route = Northwest Ridge (same PCT approach from the north side); West Route has no independent identity (the west summit is what the Northwest Ridge reaches, and a west-ridge descent is a variant at most). I could not read the stored text of these rows (four are empty shells), so the pairing rests on the names and grades alone: East Class 2, North Class 3, NW Ridge Class 3, SE Spur Class 2+, West Class 2.
recommendation: KEEP two rows, MERGE the rest. Keep 'Northwest Ridge' (to the true summit) and 'Southeast Spur' (East summit, rename 'Southeast Spur (East Peak)'); merge East Route into Southeast Spur and North Route into Northwest Ridge (the survivor keeps the guidebook name; if the owner prefers to keep a short-hand name, show it as an alias); mark 'West Route' unconfirmed and delete unless the owner knows of a west line (a ridge descent toward Windy Pass is the only west variation seen, and no source calls it a route). Also: all five are stored discipline 'alpine' with Class 2-3 grades; under the owner's rule they are 'scrambling' (non-technical, never roped). Our AREA pin (47.34769,-121.4495) sits on the lower EAST summit (34 m from Peakbagger's 'East Peak'); the true high point is the west summit, about 400 m west-northwest at roughly 47.3492,-121.4547 (taken from three recent summiting GPS logs, not from a map, so confirm before storing). Track assignment: no packet track attaches to a row as-is because the Tinkham logs mostly link Silver/Abiel (3394699 and 3228083 high-point near 47.3616,-121.4613 = Silver Peak); logs 3394676 (1 Nov 2026) and 3368547 (27 Sep 2026) go to the Tinkham summits from the Mirror Lake trailhead and could be tested against the southeast spur / loop once the row is filled.

southeast_spur_fill.name: Southeast Spur (East Peak)
southeast_spur_fill.best_season: July through October; the boot path is often snow-covered into June
southeast_spur_fill.overview: The easy way onto Tinkham: a short, steep boot path from the south end of Mirror Lake straight up the southeast spur to the lower east summit. The true high point, the west summit, is a few minutes along an easy ridge. Often combined with the Northwest Ridge for a loop.
southeast_spur_fill.approach: Start at the Mirror Lake trailhead at the end of Forest Road 5480 (about 3,600 ft). Hike the Mirror Lake trail to the lake, mostly level, then follow the PCT to the lake's south end and find the boot path.
southeast_spur_fill.beta: The path climbs about 1,200 ft in just over a mile through grass and talus on the southeast spur, with no exposure. From the east summit continue west along the ridge to the true high point; the ridge is easy and takes a few minutes. Return the same way or drop to the PCT by the Northwest Ridge boot path.

proposed.area_pin_note: Move the area pin to the west summit once a mapped coordinate is confirmed; current pin is the east summit.
